question: Nursing informatics brings together three main fields. Which ones are they?

options.A: Nursing administration, data entry, and software design
options.B: Public health, statistics, and medical engineering
options.D: Nursing science, computer science, and information science

explanation: Think of nursing informatics as a bridge! It combines nursing practice with computer and information sciences so we can manage health data easily and care for patients better. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why is using digital health records often better than old-fashioned paper notes?

options.A: It makes patient information quickly accessible across different departments
options.B: It prevents patients from asking questions about their treatment plan
options.C: It guarantees that medical errors will never happen during a shift
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for nurses to write assessment notes

explanation: Digital records let doctors and nurses view and update patient info instantly. No more waiting for paper charts to be brought down the hall! [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is the main job of an Electronic Health Record (EHR) in the hospital?

options.A: Tracking hospital supply inventory and ordering new medical equipment
options.B: Managing staff work schedules and payroll calculations
options.C: Providing entertainment options for clients staying overnight
options.D: Serving as a digital version of a client's comprehensive medical chart

explanation: An EHR is simply your patient's complete medical history, lab results, and notes kept safely in one digital folder. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h2)

question: How do Electronic Health Records help different healthcare workers team up better?

options.A: By automatically assigning daily nursing tasks to the available staff on duty
options.B: By restricting access to client files to only one department at a time
options.C: By allowing authorized clinicians from various specialties to review up-to-date findings instantly
options.D: By replacing verbal shift handovers with automated text messages

explanation: When everyone can see the latest test results and notes right away, the whole care team stays on the same page without delays. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is the main goal of a Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS)?

options.A: To monitor hospital room temperatures and environmental safety
options.B: To provide targeted recommendations and safety alerts based on client data
options.C: To schedule client appointments and manage billing operations
options.D: To automatically diagnose complex diseases without physician input

explanation: A CDSS is like a smart assistant on the computer that gives helpful pop-ups, like drug allergy warnings, to keep your patient safe. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h3)

question: You enter a medication order into the computer, and a warning pops up about a bad drug interaction. What should you do next?

options.A: Ignore the pop-up window because computers frequently make mistakes
options.B: Turn off the computer system to prevent further alerts from showing up
options.C: Administer the medication immediately since the computer cannot override a doctor
options.D: Investigate the warning, verify the client's profile, and consult the prescribing physician

explanation: Always treat these alerts as a helpful safety net! Pause, double-check the patient and the order, and talk to the doctor before giving the drug. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h3)

question: What does a Barcode Medication Administration (BCMA) system help you check before giving drugs to a patient?

options.A: The insurance coverage approval status for the specific prescription
options.B: The current market cost of the prescribed pharmaceutical drug
options.C: The correct matching of the nurse, client, and medication package
options.D: The exact manufacturing date of the syringe or intravenous tubing

explanation: BCMA scanners are great tools. They scan your badge, the patient's wristband, and the drug packet to make sure it's the right drug for the right person! [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why do hospitals prefer Computerized Provider Order Entry (CPOE) over handwriting prescriptions on paper?

options.A: It allows nurses to change medication dosages without a doctor's approval
options.B: It ensures that clients never experience side effects from medications
options.C: It eliminates dangerous transcription errors caused by messy handwriting
options.D: It speeds up the physical manufacturing of pills in the hospital pharmacy

explanation: Typed orders mean no more guessing what a doctor wrote, preventing mistakes from unclear handwriting or confusing abbreviations. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h4)

question: What is the biggest advantage of Remote Patient Monitoring for patients staying at home?

options.A: It transmits vital physiological data directly to healthcare facilities
options.B: It provides free internet service to households in rural communities
options.C: It replaces the need for personal hygiene assistance from family caregivers
options.D: It cures chronic illnesses automatically without medication intervention

explanation: Patients can check things like blood pressure at home, and the readings go straight to the clinic so nurses can keep an eye on them. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h5)

question: How do telehealth and remote monitoring help keep patients out of the hospital?

options.A: By eliminating all potential health risks associated with aging at home
options.B: By allowing nurses to catch early signs of clinical deterioration and intervene quickly
options.C: By stopping clients from taking prescribed medications incorrectly
options.D: By forcing clients to visit the outpatient clinic every single day

explanation: Catching small changes early means the care team can step in and fix things before a minor issue turns into an emergency. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h5)

question: Which of these actions breaks patient data privacy rules in a digital hospital?

options.A: Sharing your computer login password with a fellow nurse who forgot theirs
options.B: Discussing a client's lab results inside a private consultation room
options.C: Reviewing the medical history of an assigned client during your shift
options.D: Logging out of the electronic health record workstation before walking away

explanation: Never share your password! If someone else uses your login, you are responsible for any changes made in that patient's file. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h6)

question: What does the term 'digital divide' mean in modern healthcare?

options.A: The difference between paper medical records and electronic health records
options.B: Disagreements between doctors and nurses over which software program to use
options.C: Inequality in access to technology and internet services among different populations
options.D: The technical separation between hospital database servers and clinic computers

explanation: The digital divide happens when some patients lack smartphones, computers, or good internet, making it hard for them to use telehealth services. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h6)

question: What is 'alert fatigue' when nurses deal with hospital computers?

options.A: Experiencing physical exhaustion from working long night shifts on a computer
options.B: Growing tired of attending mandatory computer training classes every year
options.C: Feeling overwhelmed by the bright display screens used in hospital monitors
options.D: Becoming desensitized to frequent warning pop-ups and ignoring important prompts

explanation: When computers give too many minor warnings all day, nurses start ignoring them—which can be dangerous if a real emergency alert pops up! [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is the best way to get nursing staff to happily accept and use new hospital software?

options.A: Punishing nurses who express frustration or make mistakes during the transition
options.B: Involving frontline nurses in the software selection and workflow design process
options.C: Replacing all computers with paper charts if the first day of training is difficult
options.D: Requiring staff to figure out the new computer program entirely on their own

explanation: When bedside nurses help choose and test the software from the start, the system actually fits everyday hospital needs and is much easier to use. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h7)
